decision_note: Book chapter/preprint reviews invasive plants as novel food resources from the pollinator perspective; it does not provide a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response for SCH screening.
Primary Silene latifolia study evaluates a native Hadena moth that both pollinates and consumes developing seeds; retain for nursery-pollinator benefit-cost/role-boundary adjudication.
Ant-hemipteran mutualism dissertation concerns defensive ants, hemipterans and broader invertebrate community effects on honey mesquite; no focal pollinator service/response is measured.

Fig/fig-wasp thesis directly examines stability and conflict in an obligate pollination mutualism where wasp reproduction and seed production share fig flowers, with additional non-pollinating wasp pressures; retain for coupled mutualism-conflict adjudication.

Repository/pre-publication record for the Erica bee-avoidance study measuring floral conspicuousness, bird pollination and bee nectar robbing; retain and resolve report dependence with SCHPRISMA-000464 at full text.
Published Erica study tests floral conspicuousness against bird pollination and bee nectar robbing across multiple species/populations; retain for floral-signal pollinator-robber adjudication.
Floral silicon survey quantifies tissue silicon across taxa; pollination and herbivore defence are motivating hypotheses rather than measured ecological receiver responses in the focal study.
Annals of Botany commentary on green-flower visibility is not an independent primary study or focused SCH synthesis.

Primary Salvia brachyodon study links fragmented-pollinator communities, effective pollinator loss, pollen/nectar robbers, mating-system change and resource allocation; retain for pollinator-exploiter and evolutionary-response adjudication.

Dissertation explicitly studies landscape and domestication effects on multi-trophic interactions in berry systems, including pollination and plant defence/herbivore channels; retain for chapter-level primary-source and independence adjudication.
Faba-bean landscape study measures bumblebee visitation, pollination benefit and productivity but no focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Landscape crop-diversity study measures crop pollinators, pollination benefit and yield without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
Landscape conservation-measure study concerns wild-bee density and richness rather than a plant trait with pollinator and antagonist responses.
Preprint on latitudinal flowering-schedule clines measures heritable phenology; pollinator competition and herbivory are inferred environmental explanations rather than measured receiver responses.
Published version of the latitudinal flowering-schedule study measures adaptive phenology clines but does not directly measure pollinator and antagonist responses to the floral coordinate.

Primary Palicourea experiment shows foliar herbivory changes floral traits/rewards, reduces hummingbird and bee visitation and lowers fruit set; retain for herbivory-induced pollinator-mediated fitness adjudication.
Primary Manduca study tests how induced leaf state alters adult pollinator behaviour and larval herbivore performance in a pollinating-herbivore life cycle; retain for coupled-role adjudication.
Aquilegia experiment compares legitimate visitors and nectar robbers, but the focal response is nectar bacterial community assembly rather than a plant floral trait or plant reproductive outcome.
Focused review of linalool explicitly synthesizes floral attraction of pollinators and defence against herbivores/pathogens; retain as relevant synthesis/source-chasing material.

Primary/model-based plant-pollinator network study explicitly contrasts trait complementarity for pollination with barriers to floral exploitation across empirical networks; retain for architecture/source-boundary adjudication.
Centrosema thesis directly links florivory/herbivory to pollinator visitation, floral traits, seed set and selection implications; retain for herbivory-pollination fitness adjudication.

Primary Campanula study shows efficient pollinators increase reproduction whereas small bees deplete pollen and exacerbate pollen limitation, acting as functional exploiters; retain for consumer-role boundary adjudication.

Dissertation explicitly studies bee pollination, ant seed predation and crop yield under local-management and landscape contexts; retain for chapter-level service-disservice/common-yield adjudication.
